title: Login password input is unmasked
description: cmd/resy-snipe/login.go:131 reads the password via promptRaw (a bufio.Reader.ReadString wrapper), which echoes the password to the terminal as the user types. golang.org/x/term is already a transitive dependency; term.ReadPassword on a TTY gives a no-echo prompt.
acceptance_criteria: Password input does not echo when stdin is a TTY; non-TTY input (test harness, scripted) still works through the existing bufio path; cmd/resy-snipe/login_test.go remains green.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 1a6519f: added promptPassword using term.ReadPassword on TTY, bufio fallback for tests.

title: Parser breaks on Resy /4/find venue.id shape change
description: Resy now returns `venue.id` as an object `{"resy": <int>}` on /4/find, but FindVenueIdent.ID was typed as int64. Live snipe fails at first poll with: `json: cannot unmarshal object into Go struct field FindVenueIdent.results.venues.venue.id of type int64`. Confirmed against live API (Astoria DC, 2026-05-25) — booking the rest of the flow works once parsing succeeds.
acceptance_criteria: FindVenueIdent.ID parses both legacy bare-int and new object-form shapes without binding the code to either; resy package tests still pass; live snipe completes the full submitted->booked path.
notes: Fix landed in this session: changed FindVenueIdent.ID to json.RawMessage in internal/resy/types.go since the field is never read downstream. Tests in anti_bot_test.go / errors_test.go / book_test.go / integration_test.go that use the bare-int shape continue to parse.
close_reason: Fixed in commit fc94d9b: dropped unused FindVenueIdent.ID field so JSON decoder ignores the shape change.

title: resy-snipe doctor: pre-flight validation before commit-time
description: Right now you discover failure at the moment of truth — at midnight, the snipe fires, the session is expired, the payment method got deleted, the anti-bot signer binary moved, the venue id is wrong. `resy-snipe doctor <same flags as snipe>` should run a dry pre-flight: validate session (Ping /2/user), verify at least one valid payment method on file, resolve the venue, smoke-test the anti-bot signer if configured (a Sign call against a fake payload), and confirm the wall-clock release window is in the future. Output: a checklist with pass/fail per check and a single overall verdict.
acceptance_criteria: Returns exit code 0 only when ALL checks pass; per-check stdout shows clear pass/fail + remediation hint; `resy-snipe doctor` (no flags) runs the subset of checks that don't need an intent (session, signer); integration test asserts a doctored intent that subsequently snipe-runs without setup-class errors.
notes: Cheap insurance and a great pre-snipe ritual. Reuses the existing client.Ping, resolver, and signer infrastructure — almost zero new code in the adapter layer; the work is in cmd/resy-snipe/doctor.go assembly.

title: Resy URL → snipe (paste-and-go ergonomics)
description: resolver.ParseResyURL already exists and is wired into the `venue resolve` subcommand. The snipe path (cmd/resy-snipe/main.go + intent.go) still requires `-venue-id <numeric>` which means the user has to manually look up an ID before they can snipe. Plumb URL parsing into the snipe flag set: `-venue <url-or-slug-or-id>` accepts any of the three forms, runs the resolver to land on a numeric ID, then proceeds with the existing flow.
acceptance_criteria: `resy-snipe -venue https://resy.com/cities/dc/venues/astoria-dc -res-times 19:00` works end-to-end; `-venue 49716` still works (back-compat); `-venue-id` is kept as a deprecated alias with a one-time warning; interactive mode accepts URLs in the venue prompt.

title: iMessage notifier transport
description: notify.Notifier interface exists with a stdout impl. For unattended snipes (midnight release, multi-day discover window), terminal output is the wrong notification surface. macOS iMessage via osascript is the highest-ROI single transport on the user's primary platform: send myself 'BOOKED Astoria DC 19:00 — TwBm...' the moment the state machine hits Booked.
acceptance_criteria: New notify.IMessage transport that sends a message via `osascript -e 'tell application "Messages"...'` to a configured handle (env var or config field); engine subscriber bridges Booked + Failed events to the notifier; transport degrades gracefully when not on macOS (logs warning, no panic); test covers the script-construction path without actually sending.
notes: 30-50 LOC. The shape is identical to the existing stdout notifier; only difference is the side-effect. Config: RESY_SNIPE_IMESSAGE_TO env var. Be careful with shell quoting in the osascript command — the venue/confirmation strings can contain anything.

title: Add resy-snipe status + cancel subcommands
description: Phase 1 left operability gaps: there's no way to list what's scheduled in the local store, and no way to cancel a stuck snipe without manual sqlite surgery. With Phase 2 daemon mode landing (serve subcommand already in M2), these become load-bearing. `resy-snipe status` should list snipes from store.Store with their current Status + venue + scheduled-at; `resy-snipe cancel <snipe-id>` should drive the state machine through Submitted/Scheduled/Awaiting/Finding/Booking → Canceled (Booking→Canceled is the interesting case — needs to interact with the race-and-cancel layer cleanly).
acceptance_criteria: `resy-snipe status` prints a table of active snipes (id, status, venue, scheduled_at, next-action-at) sourced from store.Store; `resy-snipe cancel <id>` transitions a non-terminal snipe to Canceled, surfacing an error if the snipe is already Booked or terminal; tests cover the Booking→Canceled path (snipe inflight + cancel arrives mid-race) and the noop cases.
notes: Mentioned in docs/work-items.md as 'Plausible next epics' but not yet filed. Engine already supports the state transitions — just needs CLI surface + a Cancel method on the engine handle.

title: Implement CompleteMFA against live Resy endpoint
description: internal/resy/auth.go:131-136 — CompleteMFA is a Phase 1 stub that returns 'not implemented'. The MFAError path in Login already detects the challenge; the endpoint shape on the completion side has never been calibrated against the live API because the test account has no MFA enrolled.
acceptance_criteria: CompleteMFA submits the challenge token + user-entered code to the real Resy MFA endpoint, parses the resulting JWT, persists the session via the SessionStore, and surfaces the same providers.Err taxonomy (ErrAuthExpired on bad code, ErrMFARequired on continued challenge, etc.). Integration test against a recorded response.
notes: Blocker: needs an MFA-enrolled Resy account to capture the request/response shape. Can't be implemented blind without guessing the endpoint path and field names. Next session: either enroll MFA on a throwaway account, or capture from a packet trace of the Resy web flow.

title: Prepaid/ticketed venue support (Stripe-backed events)
description: Some Resy venues (tasting menus, ticketed events) charge at booking time via a Stripe-backed flow that requires extra fields on /3/book (e.g. cart_id, ticket selections, prepayment amount). Current book.go only handles the standard card-on-file no-show coverage shape — prepayment venues fail at booking->booked with a parse or 4xx error.
acceptance_criteria: /3/book handler detects prepaid venue shape from /3/details response, surfaces the prepayment amount + ticket selection back to the user for explicit consent (no surprise charges), passes through the Stripe payment intent fields. Live-tested against at least one prepayment venue.
notes: Needs capture of a real prepayment-venue /3/details + /3/book request/response shape to calibrate against — same blocker shape as MFA work.

title: Hardcoded payment_methods[0] selection with no surface
description: internal/resy/book.go:88 and book.go:134 and prepare.go:62 all unconditionally pick the user's first payment method from /3/details. Multiple cards on file → always charges/holds against the default. No CLI flag, no selection UX, no per-snipe override.
acceptance_criteria: User can specify a payment method via CLI flag or per-snipe config (by display name or last-4); resy adapter passes the chosen method id to /3/book; tests cover both default-fallback and explicit-selection paths.
